text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Suleyman Demirel and Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller say that Turkey's republican system will be ruined by anti-democratic interventions, in a reference to rumours of a military coup.
- Parliament will vote on a leftist opposition censure motion to topple the Islamist-led government on Tuesday.
- Demirel says blackout campaign to pressurise the government over security scandal is legal.
- Head of Turkish armed forces goes on a visit to Israel on Monday which is both military and political.
- This week's National Security Council meeting with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will be tough as the armed forces will mention their concern over anti-secular movements.
- Pro-secularist statements of the number two in armed forces during visit to the United States greeted favourably in Turkey.
- Defence ministry had stepped up a project that open the way for private sector to enter into defence industry in next 10 years.
- Two firemen die in hospital after being injured while fighting a fire on Turkey's biggest oil tanker in an Istanbul earlier this month.
